title: Cost Sweeper: Console playback & reversible apply timeline for batching/caching recommendations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a Console UX surface that enables engineers and platform owners to preview, simulate, safely apply, and unwind batching and caching optimization suggestions. This ticket covers the recommendation card design, config diff preview UI, canary/staged rollout controls, and an immutable apply audit ledger.

Scope:
- Recommendation card layout with estimated token savings, latency impact, confidence score, and suggested config patch (batching/window/kv-cache TTL, quantization profile).
- Diff preview screen that shows before/after YAML/json snippets with inline explanation of semantics and risk flags.
- 'Simulate' dry-run that runs a sandboxed evaluator to show estimated throughput and error regression risk (integration point: evaluate-service).
- Canary/staged apply controls: percentage rollout, duration, automatic rollback thresholds (latency or error rate), manual kill switch.
- Apply history / audit ledger: who applied, when, what inputs, snapshots, rollbacks, and links to relevant PRs/dashboards.
- Searchable/filterable ledger and card list by model, pool, tag, and customer tenant.
- Exportable audit entries (CSV/JSON) and retention policy (90 days default, configurable).

Out of scope: backend autoscaling policy changes (ENG task), RBAC role gating (separate compliance epic).
acceptance_criteria:
- Designers deliver high-fidelity cards + diff preview and canary control mocks approved by PM and Eng.
- Frontend implements interactive cards, preview modal, and rollback UI.
- Backend exposes endpoints for simulate/dry-run and apply with event audit log entries created for every apply/rollback.
- Canary applies enforce automatic rollback when monitored metrics cross thresholds; alerting wired to paging and console notifications.
- Audit log searchable and exportable in Console and immutable for configured retention period.
- End-to-end smoke test showing a simulated apply then a safe rollback within the staging environment.
